USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

Supporting fracture healing: 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient wants to improve modifiable factors after a fracture and reports daily smoking. The clinician discusses a factor associated with impaired healing and offers support. Which intervention directly addresses this important behavioral risk?

  1. Individualized medication review
  2. Smoking cessation support
  3. Adequate protein and micronutrient intake
  4. Appropriate mechanical stability
  5. Adequate blood supply
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Smoking cessation support

Smoking is an important modifiable risk factor for impaired fracture healing.

Understanding the options

Smoking cessation support
Smoking is an important modifiable risk factor for impaired fracture healing.
Adequate protein and micronutrient intake
Healing needs adequate nutrition; correcting deficiency is more defensible than promising benefit from excessive supplementation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Appropriate mechanical stability
Nutrition cannot compensate for inadequate fracture stability. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Adequate blood supply
Biological healing requires viable perfused tissue as well as mechanical support. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Individualized medication review
The risks and benefits of medicines during healing should be reviewed; prescribed drugs should not be stopped indiscriminately. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
